events.excerpt: The ESP32-P4 is Espressif’s high-end application processor, with two blistering fast RISC-V cores for a surprisingly reasonable price. As it’s a very capable computer in its own right, there have been a range of operating systems made for it. Latest among them is [Jthwho]’s BMDS, for Bare Metal Do Stuff , which targets an Olimex board. At its heart is the FreeRTOS kernel we’ve seen in so many other similar projects, but on top is an OS which is described as being like DOS in its one-user minimally intrusive operation. It runs ELF binaries, and has some POSIX compliance, with BusyBox being a port. Perhaps most noticeable is its GUI, which provides a very slick desktop straight out of the late 1990s. We can see that had this appeared as a contemporary of Amigas, 68k Macs, and Windows 3.x, it would have immediately been a real contender. But the question is, does such an OS have a niche here in 2026? We think it might, as this processor is slowly establishing itself in a new genre of powerful machines aimed at hackers and tinkerers. Either way it’s an impressive achievement, and we look forward to seeing it develop over time.
events.headline: A Desktop OS for the ESP32-P4

events.excerpt: What if you could see sound? A Chladni plate uses a speaker and small particles, like sand, to give you a visual representation of sound, and [CrazyScience] shows you how to make one. The plate dates back to 1787, created by the eponymous physicist. Of course, back then, there were no speakers, so the original plate was metal with a violin bow raked across the edges. The modern version uses an ESP32, a speaker, and salt. The patterns depend on the resonance points of the plate. The device has a rotary encoder to tune different frequencies. Check it out in the video below. There’s also an OLED display to show the frequency and patterns. There is also a 3D-printed enclosure. The patterns, of course, depend on standing waves. We aren’t sure that there’s any practical value for it, but we like the way it looks. This isn’t the first time we’ve talked about Chladni . Visualizing things before the CRT was interesting, to say the least.

events.excerpt: In a significant update to its guidelines for prostate cancer screening, the American Cancer Society is now recommending that men get routinely screened for prostate cancer with a PSA test. Men at average risk should get a PSA test every two years from age 50 to 69, according to the new guidelines released Thursday. Men considered at high risk due to race and family history should start testing earlier, at 45, and most are recommended to get tested every year. Specifically, yearly testing starting at age 45 is recommended for all Black men, who have higher rates of prostate cancer. Non-Black men should also get yearly testing starting at 45 if a close relative was diagnosed with prostate cancer before age 65, or if more than one of their relatives has had prostate cancer. On the other hand, if only one close relative was diagnosed with prostate cancer and it was diagnosed at age 65 or older, non-Black men in this case should start PSA screening at 45, but are recommended to get testing only every two years. events.excerpt: Bitcoin Magazine DOJ’s Operation TorNado Arrests 354 and Seizes $234 Million in Cash and Crypto The Justice Department and Europol said Thursday that Operation TorNado has produced 354 arrests and the seizure of more than $234 million in cash and virtual currencies, in what the FBI called the largest takedown yet of dark web drug vendors and buyers. The announcement came from the department’s Joint Criminal Opioid and Darknet Enforcement team, or JCODE, an FBI-led group created in 2018. Officials said Operation TorNado is the sixth, and most extensive, internationally coordinated action since then, and that it builds on last year’s Operation RapTor. The sweep ran from May 2025 to October 2026. Europol, which coordinated work with agencies in 14 countries, published a parallel statement the same day. The operation targeted vendors and buyers who had been active on five dark web markets already seized by law enforcement: Archetyp, Bohemia, Nemesis, Kingdom and Tor2Door. Officials also identified accounts on DrugHub and on forums, single-vendor shops and encrypted messaging services. The seizures included about 5.7 metric tons of illicit drugs worldwide, among them fentanyl and other opioids, methamphetamine, heroin, cocaine, ecstasy and MDMA, plus 38 pill presses and 209 firearms.
